- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 95+ → forecast 100+), then fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated: model fails to recognize that prices often revert to prior 10–15 day averages after strong moves.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are consistently too high, suggesting model overreacts to recent volatility.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends — often misses early signs of price drop and continues upward bias.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to “herd” overestimation when history shows consolidation or decline.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model still forecasts upward, especially if recent values are above 90.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <80) — tends to smooth out sharp drops, leading to false stability.
- Forecasts often ignore seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-month dips, quarterly adjustments) — model assumes linear continuation.
